item.text:
{
  "artifact_id": "LIVE-TEACH-CLAMP-concepts",
  "revision": "r1",
  "task_id": "LIVE-TEACH-CLAMP",
  "task_revision": "t1",
  "type": "ConceptSet",
  "scope": "Teaching concept enumeration and verification planning for a bench clamp intended to hold a workpiece without damage. Uses the supplied proposed functional model and morphological-analysis method. All implementation principles below are teaching hypotheses, not customer requirements or demonstrated solutions. No preferred concept, approved specification, prototype execution or engineering validation is established. The lunar-sampling case supplies no clamp performance evidence and contributes no parameters to these concepts.",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "id": "C01",
      "text": "The task specifies a bench clamp and the desired outcome of holding a workpiece without damage.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "evidence_refs": []
    },
    {
      "id": "C02",
      "text": "Customer loads, workpiece material, geometry, allowable movement and damage criteria remain unknown. REQ01 and REQ02 remain proposed; their hardness is unknown.",
      "kind": "unknown",
      "evidence_refs": []
    },
    {
      "id": "C03",
      "text": "F01 establishes contact; F02 applies restraint; F03 maintains restraint; F04 manages contact effects; F05 releases restraint; F06 assesses workpiece condition. These allocations remain modeling proposals from the supplied FunctionModel.",
      "kind": "assumption",
      "evidence_refs": []
    },
    {
      "id": "C04",
      "text": "Manual input, pneumatic supply, fixed-reference contact and external inspection are alternative teaching assumptions. None is established as available or acceptable for the customer.",
      "kind": "assumption",
      "evidence_refs": []
    },
    {
      "id": "C05",
      "text": "The proposed contact-management option is a hypothesis to investigate; distributing contact does not by itself establish adequate retention or freedom from damage.",
      "kind": "assumption",
      "evidence_refs": []
    }
  ],
  "evidence_refs": [],
  "payload": {
    "function_ids": [
      "F01",
      "F02",
      "F03",
      "F04",
      "F05",
      "F06"
    ],
    "options": [
      {
        "id": "O01",
        "function_id": "F01",
        "principle": "Establish workpiece contact against a fixed reference before applying restraint.",
        "conditions": [
          "Teaching hypothesis derived from the method example.",
          "Requires compatible workpiece geometry, accessible contact regions and a reaction path to the support; all remain unknown."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O02",
        "function_id": "F02",
        "principle": "Convert manual rotation through a screw transmission into closing displacement and restraint.",
        "conditions": [
          "Manual operation is an assumption, not a customer constraint.",
          "Operator input, travel, transmission geometry and resulting contact forces require definition."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O03",
        "function_id": "F02",
        "principle": "Use a pneumatic cylinder to produce closing displacement and restraint.",
        "conditions": [
          "Pneumatic supply availability and acceptability are unknown.",
          "For the exclusion example only, assume a single-direction closing cylinder with no screw transmission.",
          "Pressure, stroke, control and support interfaces remain unspecified."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O04",
        "function_id": "F03",
        "principle": "Investigate retaining the screw position through transmission resistance after manual input stops.",
        "conditions": [
          "Position retention is a hypothesis, not an established self-locking property.",
          "Requires review of transmission geometry, friction, disturbances, load duration and support reactions."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O05",
        "function_id": "F03",
        "principle": "Investigate maintaining restraint through sustained pneumatic input.",
        "conditions": [
          "Continuous supply and control are assumed for this teaching route.",
          "Leakage, supply loss, movement and required holding duration remain unresolved."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O06",
        "function_id": "F04",
        "principle": "Investigate distributing restraint over a defined contact region to manage local workpiece effects.",
        "conditions": [
          "Proposed interpretation of F04, not an evidenced damage-prevention solution.",
          "Contact area, material, surface interaction and deformation require definition.",
          "Any effect on slip resistance must be evaluated together with damage."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O07",
        "function_id": "F05",
        "principle": "Reverse the same screw transmission to withdraw contact and release restraint.",
        "conditions": [
          "Requires an actual reversible screw transmission connected to the moving contact.",
          "Release travel, residual contact and removal clearance remain unknown."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O08",
        "function_id": "F05",
        "principle": "Investigate elastic return after pneumatic closing input is removed.",
        "conditions": [
          "Requires a return element and a defined pressure-release path.",
          "Return force, sticking, release travel and behavior during unintended supply loss remain unknown.",
          "Compatibility with sustained holding must be investigated."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "id": "O09",
        "function_id": "F06",
        "principle": "Allocate before-and-after workpiece condition assessment to an external operator or inspection resource.",
        "conditions": [
          "Supporting verification activity rather than a specified built-in sensing mechanism.",
          "Requires an agreed reference condition, damage criterion, inspection method and responsible reviewer.",
          "No assessment has been performed."
        ],
        "evidence_refs": []
      }
    ],
    "combinations": [
      {
        "id": "M01",
        "option_ids": [
          "O01",
          "O02",
          "O04",
          "O06",
          "O07",
          "O09"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Manual screw route covers all six proposed functions: reference contact, screw closing, hypothesized position retention, contact management, reverse-screw release and external assessment. The screw supplies a conceptual connection between closing and release, but holding behavior, contact effects and bench reactions remain unknown. Manual operation and reverse travel introduce operator and clearance dependencies. Retained for investigation only; no recommendation is supported."
      },
      {
        "id": "M02",
        "option_ids": [
          "O01",
          "O03",
          "O05",
          "O06",
          "O08",
          "O09"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Pneumatic route covers all six proposed functions through reference contact, pneumatic closing, sustained input, contact management, elastic return and external assessment. It adds supply, control and return-element dependencies. Whether pressure can maintain restraint while permitting intentional release, including behavior after supply loss, remains unresolved. No recommendation is supported."
      },
      {
        "id": "M03",
        "option_ids": [
          "O01",
          "O03",
          "O05",
          "O06",
          "O07",
          "O09"
        ],
        "status": "excluded",
        "reason": "Under the explicit O03 topology assumption of a closing cylinder without a screw transmission, O07 cannot release restraint by reversing that absent transmission. This is a conditional logical conflict, not an empirical performance judgment. Adding a screw would require a newly defined option and combination."
      }
    ],
    "compatibility": [
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O02",
          "O07"
        ],
        "status": "compatible",
        "reason": "At the stated principle level only, forward and reverse operation refer to the same reversible screw transmission. This conditional connection establishes neither release clearance nor overall feasibility.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O02",
          "O04"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Screw-driven closing does not establish that position or restraint will persist after input stops; transmission and disturbance conditions are missing.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O03",
          "O07"
        ],
        "status": "incompatible",
        "reason": "O03 explicitly excludes a screw transmission for this topology, whereas O07 requires that transmission as the release mechanism.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O03",
          "O05",
          "O08"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Closing, sustained holding and elastic return require a coordinated pressure and motion sequence. Available supply, intentional venting, return force and input-loss behavior are undefined.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O01",
          "O02",
          "O04",
          "O06",
          "O07",
          "O09"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Whole-route check for M01 remains open: contact geometry, force transmission, restraint persistence, support reactions, release and assessment must jointly satisfy retention and damage criteria that are not yet defined.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      },
      {
        "option_ids": [
          "O01",
          "O03",
          "O05",
          "O06",
          "O08",
          "O09"
        ],
        "status": "unknown",
        "reason": "Whole-route check for M02 remains open: supply and return behavior interact with contact forces, restraint continuity, support reactions and damage. Pairwise consistency cannot resolve these system interactions.",
        "evidence_refs": []
      }
    ],
    "unknowns": [
      "Confirm the intended operation, operator capabilities and available actuation resources before comparing manual and pneumatic routes.",
      "Obtain workpiece materials, finishes, geometries and variation; then plan contact and clearance review for engagement, holding and release.",
      "Establish loads, directions, duration and allowable movement; then plan restraint and bench-reaction analysis for each retained route.",
      "Agree damage criteria and inspection methods with the responsible stakeholder before planning before-and-after assessment.",
      "Investigate whether retention and acceptable contact effects can coexist; no acceptable force range has been established.",
      "For M01, plan review of screw position retention, disturbance sensitivity and release behavior once transmission and load conditions are available.",
      "For M02, define the supply, control and return sequence; then plan walkthroughs of intentional release, supply loss and incomplete release.",
      "Identify requirement owners, confirmation authority and hard constraints. Unknown hard gates prevent recommendation or unique selection.",
      "No approved comparison baseline exists. After requirements are clarified, use the same workpiece, load, movement and damage criteria for both routes; compare operator effort, resource dependence and interface complexity without inventing scores.",
      "Prototype and verification activities remain proposals only. Define representative workpieces, resources, procedures and acceptance limits before any later execution; no tests, measurements or acceptance results are supplied."
    ]
  }
}
